answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a small refundable stake that is slashed when peers prove duplicate behavior, so one operator running a thousand sockpuppets pays a thousand times the cost of a single honest agent. A shared atlas of stake and reputation lets verifiers spot clusters acting in lockstep, like a mesa of identical footprints on an otherwise varied plain. Honest agents earn a beacon of attested work history over time, so cheap fresh identities cannot outvote established ones without first doing real, costly work.
